sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1977 [dated July 1976]. Introduction, incl. 'Regional variations in the pronunciation of Kâte' (pp. xxiii-xxvi). In W. Flierl & H. Strauss (eds), Kâte dictionary, Pacific Linguistics C-41. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Kinalakna stress or tone. First-hand segmental remarks only: Kinalakna belongs to the 'Western group' with syllables closed by m n ŋ p t k, dental (not alveolar) plosives and nasals, a five-vowel system (no sixth vowel â), no p/f distinction and no affricate series distinct from s/z. The stress rule given on p. xx ('The first syllable of a word always carries the heaviest stress') is explicitly about Kâte, not Kinalakna.
